blocks.text: Where an internal auditor's day goes

The research I could find does not break an auditor's week into hours. The clearest audit-specific source is a 2021 brief from The Institute of Internal Auditors, based on a survey with Diligent. It says too much time is spent on audit reporting, follow-up and collecting evidence. The brief gives no percentages, so read it as direction, not measurement.

The same brief says those reporting, follow-up and evidence tasks can be automated to free time for advisory work. It also says remote work has increased internal audit workload and reduced important water cooler moments. Fewer quick conversations mean more of the job lives in files and inboxes.

Microsoft's Work Trend Index covers knowledge workers in general, not internal auditors. It found the average employee spends 57% of their time communicating in meetings, email and chat. The other 43% goes to creating work in documents, spreadsheets and presentations. That window was the 28 days ending March 2023, for Microsoft 365 commercial users.

Microsoft's June 2025 study surveyed 31,000 knowledge workers across 31 markets. It found an average of 117 emails and 153 Teams messages received per person per day. It also counted about 275 interruptions a day from meetings, email or chat notifications. Auditors were not reported as their own group. Measure your own week before you trust any average, including these.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics groups accountants and auditors into one profile. It counts 1,595,200 jobs in 2025 and a median pay of $83,680 for May 2025. The profile says internal auditors work to find and eliminate waste, fraud and other financial risks. BLS does not split out internal auditors in these numbers.
What an AI assistant for internal auditors can do for you

Lazur helps in a small set of ways. Each one matches a question you already ask during a test. It works in whatever app you have open, and it answers out loud. It only looks at your screen while you hold ⌥ ⌘.

items: Explain: ask what a formula error, a policy line or a system message means while you look at it.
Point: ask where a tab, column or button is. Lazur circles it and labels it on your screen.
Guide: ask how to do a task. Lazur walks you one click at a time and waits for each click.
Dictate: hold fn and speak. Clean, formatted text appears at the cursor in any app.
Draft: ask for a first version of a finding, a status note or a follow-up email.
Research: send a question to run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs. It returns a summary and a report.
Everyday: set reminders, calendar events and timers, take notes, and open apps or links by voice.

blocks.text: Lazur does not do the audit for you. It does not pick a sample, rate a control or sign off a conclusion. Those calls stay with you and your audit manager. Think of Lazur as a fast colleague who answers questions about the screen in front of you. It never takes the pen.
Dictating walkthrough notes and findings

Dictation suits walkthrough notes. You speak the facts as you see them, then tidy the wording later. Hold fn, speak, and release. The text lands at the cursor in Word, Outlook or any other app that takes typed input. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots help with phrases you repeat, such as your standard opening line for a finding.
Excel for internal auditors on Mac: evidence, samples and reconciliations

Excel holds most audit evidence. You use it for samples, reconciliations and exception lists. When you hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask a question, Lazur looks at the sheet in front of you. It can point at the column with the approval date, or explain why a total is off by a few rows. For more detail, read [Excel for internal auditors on Mac](/for/internal-auditors/excel).

Excel for Mac got two changes in its October 2026 update. Naming tables at creation is now generally available on Mac. The clean-data skill and skill builder are generally available on all platforms, including Mac. The skill recorder is for Insiders on Mac only. Microsoft's post lists no ribbon or menu moves for Mac in that update.

blocks.text: Word and Outlook for findings and follow-up email

Word for Mac holds the finding text. The Review tab has the tools you need most. Use Review > New Comment to flag a sentence for your manager. Use Review > Compare to see what changed between two drafts. For the steps, read [how to compare two documents in Word on Mac](/how-to/compare-two-documents-in-word).

Outlook for Mac changed in version 16.114. Its left rail can now show supported Microsoft 365 apps. You can also pick a supported third-party online meeting provider when you create a calendar event. Microsoft's release notes list 16.114 as released October 14, 2026. The latest listed release is 16.114.3, from October 27, 2026. Check yours in Outlook > About Outlook before you ask for steps.
A worked example: from an exception to a follow-up email

Say you test payments for approval before release. Your Excel export shows one payment with an approver but no approval date. You suspect the date was stored as text. Here is how a session with Lazur can go.

items: Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the approval date column is. Lazur circles the header.
Ask why the cell looks blank. Lazur can explain that a date stored as text sorts and filters differently from a real date, and suggest checking the cell format.
Confirm the real date in the source system. Do not rely on the export alone.
Hold fn and dictate the condition in plain words, such as the approval came after release.
Ask Lazur to draft the request to payables. Add the evidence you still need and the deadline you set.
Read the draft aloud. Cut any sentence you cannot support from the file.

blocks.title: Check your data rules first
blocks.text: Audit files often hold personal and confidential data. Your audit charter and your employer's data rules decide what may appear on screen. When in doubt, use a test file or a redacted export before you hold the shortcut.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in audit work

items: Asking for a conclusion. Ask Lazur to explain, point or draft. You still rate the control and sign the finding.
Pasting client or employee data before checking your policy. Your rules come first, not the tool.
Trusting a menu you remember. Versions move, so check yours first.
Expecting Lazur to make the change. It does not click buttons or edit files. You make the change.
Skipping the check. Verify any figure Lazur reads from a sheet against the source.

blocks.text: Limits, privacy and platform support

Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Excel, Word or Outlook. It has no partnership with any app maker, and it does not operate other apps for you. It runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on the Mac.
How to start this week with an AI assistant for auditors

Pick one recurring task. A reconciliation, a status note or a meeting follow-up works well. Do it once the usual way and once with Lazur. Compare the time and the quality. Keep the method that holds up.

Lazur has a short free trial. It starts when you first open the app, and no credit card is needed. Get the app from [the download page](/download). Check [pricing](/pricing) before you pick a plan. For Word steps, see [Word for internal auditors on Mac](/for/internal-auditors/word).

faq.question: Does Lazur sit inside Excel or Word?
faq.answer: No. Lazur lives in the notch at the top of your Mac screen and works alongside the apps you already use. You switch to Excel, Word or Outlook as normal, then hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask a question.

faq.question: Can Lazur see my audit workpapers?
faq.answer: It looks at your screen only while you hold ⌥ ⌘. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer. Your audit charter and your employer's data rules decide what may appear on screen.

faq.question: Will Lazur change my Excel file for me?
faq.answer: No. It points, explains, guides and drafts. It guides you one click at a time and waits for each click, so you make every change yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur know the newest Excel and Outlook menus?
faq.answer: Check your version first in Outlook > About Outlook. Outlook 16.114 changed the left rail, and Excel's October 2026 update made naming tables at creation generally available on Mac. Lazur works from the screen in front of you, so keep the window visible when you ask.

faq.question: Can I dictate findings with it?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn, speak, and release. Clean, formatted text lands at the cursor in any app. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots help with phrases you repeat.

faq.question: Does it work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: What does Lazur cost?
faq.answer: Lazur has a short free trial with no credit card. It starts when you first open the app. Plan prices and AI action limits are on the [pricing page](/pricing), so check there before you choose a plan.

faq.question: Can I use it on live engagement files?
faq.answer: Ask your audit leader or IT team first. Many firms set their own rules for AI tools and confidential data. Lazur does not change those rules, so test on a redacted file before you use it on live work.
